rows.postTitle: Orban Was Bad, Even Though We Don't Have A Perfect Word For His Badness
rows.text:
"are these things bad and undemocratic?"

No, not under a normal definition of democracy. None of the things you listed have anything to do with political systems except the gerrymandering which is fairly common in such systems. It is a fairly standard definition of bad though. That's where I would cash out: bad but not undemocratic. This is also where I cash out about Orban.

The issue is the people using the word dictator are conflating regime type with ideology. That was always the issue and it's convenient because if you make the "liberal" in liberal democracy left wing you can endlessly say that right wingers are a threat to democracy. Democratic backsliding exists but that what is included or excluded is fairly blatantly partisan.

I have no issue holding two things at once: such experts are blatantly biased and invent entire new categories to try to attack their political opponents. And also Trump and Orban have been bad for their countries' institutions in various ways. Where I suspect I will depart from others is the socialists and Democrats have also been very bad in ways left wingers have avoided confronting. (Note: socialists is a self-description of Orban's original opposition.)

"Electoral autocracy" is just a confusion of ideology and regime type. I said at the time these people were going to be embarrassed when these regimes were just voted out of office and quietly went. First in Poland, now Hungary. It almost happened in Turkey and will eventually. My prediction was wrong only in that they're not embarrassed and have adapted the language of overthrowing a dictatorship to winning an election.

The French already have nukes that are poised to attack the United States. Though their main targets are Poland and Germany. (Seriously.)

Also: If you apply this reasoning consistently then the Chinese build up is already a non-theoretical thing that's happening. And was before Trump. Turning nuclear binary game theory into trinary is WAY more of a threat. Why is that not your bigger concern?

Given that my information is correct unless the French military is lying I'm going to give it a roughly 99% chance of being correct. French nuclear strategy is public.

French military doctrine explicitly includes rapid fire capabilities to hit the United States and has since the Cold War. It also has a doctrine of nuking allies territory if they are losing a war and feel nukes will slow down the advancing army (mostly in Germany and now Poland). It also has the "warning shot" doctrine (ultime avertissement) where French doctrine allows the use of a single nuclear weapon lower on the escalation ladder than anyone else.

That said, I agree the chances of France doing it to the US are low. On the other hand, China has been going through a massive re-armament such that we are approaching a world with three major nuclear powers. And I do think that is destabilizing.

The most important thing is to be physically attractive which is being in shape, fixing aesthetic issues (teeth, hair, skin, etc), and dressing well. The next most important thing is being in a social environment where you meet potential partners frequently. Try to gain some status in the group ideally. If you're a woman that's basically it.

If you're a man there's additional things. Firstly money and social class (which is mostly university degrees as well as certain jobs). Secondly you need to get used to approaching women and asking them out. Thirdly learn enough photography and such to have a decent dating profile.
